name: mesh-convergence
title: Adaptive mesh refinement: recovering optimal convergence on a corner singularity
question:
On the classic L-shaped-domain re-entrant-corner Laplace singularity --
where the exact solution's gradient blows up at the corner and UNIFORM
refinement is provably capped at a suboptimal convergence rate -- does a
real residual-based a posteriori error estimator, driving Doerfler-marked
ADAPTIVE refinement, concentrate elements at the corner and recover
near-optimal convergence?
hypothesis:
The L-shaped domain's re-entrant corner (interior angle 3*pi/2) has exact
harmonic solution u = r^(2/3)*sin(2*theta/3), whose H^(5/3-eps) regularity
caps P1 UNIFORM refinement's energy-norm convergence at O(dofs^-1/3)
instead of the usual O(dofs^-1/2). A residual-based edge-jump error
estimator should produce indicators that spike sharply at the corner
(where u_h's piecewise-linear gradient most disagrees with its
neighbors), so Doerfler (bulk-chasing) marking on those indicators should
concentrate new elements there and recover close to the optimal
O(dofs^-1/2) rate despite the singularity.
objective:
Run a uniform-refinement sequence and a residual-based adaptive (AMR)
sequence from the same coarse initial L-shaped mesh, fit the energy-norm-
error-vs-DOFs log-log slope for each, and confirm (a) the adaptive slope
is substantially steeper (closer to the optimal -1/2) than the uniform
slope (capped near -1/3), and (b) the adaptive mesh's cell density near
the re-entrant corner, relative to the far field, grows dramatically
relative to the initial mesh -- direct geometric evidence the estimator
is doing its job, not just producing a better number by coincidence.
description:
Real dolfinx (0.11.0) throughout -- no faking. `viva_fenics.fem_amr`
builds `Omega = [-1,1]^2 \ [0,1]x[-1,0]` via a gmsh OCC boolean cut
(re-entrant corner at the ORIGIN, distinct from `fem_gmsh`'s `"lshape"`
geometry, whose corner sits at (0.5,0.5) -- this problem needs the corner
at the origin to match the closed-form singular solution below) and
solves `-Laplacian(u) = 0` (f=0; Laplace, not Poisson) with
`u = r^(2/3)*sin(2*theta/3)` (built as a real UFL symbolic expression via
`ufl.atan2`/`ufl.sqrt`, not a numpy approximation) imposed as the
Dirichlet BC on the full domain boundary.

The a posteriori error estimator (`fem_amr.error_indicators`) is the
standard Verfurth residual estimator's edge-jump term -- for P1 elements
with f=0 the interior cell-residual term vanishes identically
(`Laplacian(u_h)=0` pointwise for piecewise-linear u_h), so
`eta_T^2 = (1/2) * sum_e h_e * ||[[du_h/dn]]||^2_{L2(e)}` over each cell's
interior edges is the whole estimator: exactly the jump in u_h's normal
derivative across each edge, which should be largest right where the
exact solution's true gradient is blowing up (`~r^-1/3`) and a
piecewise-linear field is straining hardest to track it.

`fem_amr.dorfler_mark` implements Doerfler (bulk-chasing) marking: the
smallest set of cells whose summed eta_T^2 reaches a `theta=0.5` fraction
of the total estimated error. `fem_amr.refine_marked` converts marked
cells to their edges (`dolfinx.mesh.compute_incident_entities`) and calls
real `dolfinx.mesh.refine(domain, edges=...)` -- dolfinx's Plaza/NVB
conforming refinement, which bisects the marked edges plus whatever
extra edges are needed to avoid hanging nodes. `AdaptiveRefinementStep`
(Task-2-style Step, config-driven, no time-varying inputs) runs the WHOLE
solve -> estimate -> mark -> refine loop for `n_refinements` levels and
reports the dofs/energy-error convergence history plus the final
solution; `adaptive_refinement` is its composite generator (this study's
baseline composite id). The uniform-vs-adaptive COMPARISON itself, plus
the mesh-geometry snapshots for the refinement animation, are computed
directly via `fem_amr.run_uniform_loop`/`run_amr_loop` in this study's
`sims/run.py` (the sweep/comparison logic lives in the study, not the
generator -- same convention as the investigation's other convergence
study).

Achieved result (the committed production run, `initial_h=0.3`,
`theta=0.5`, degree=1): UNIFORM refinement (7 levels, 69 -> 218,049 dofs)
fits a log-log slope of -0.338 -- matching the theoretical -1/3 (=-0.333)
almost exactly. ADAPTIVE refinement (16 levels, 69 -> 259,055 dofs) fits
a slope of -0.528 -- close to the theoretical optimal -1/2, and far
steeper than uniform's -0.338 despite starting from the identical coarse
mesh. Geometrically: the initial mesh's near-corner (r<0.15) vs far-field
(r>0.5) cell density ratio is 0.52 (i.e. actually slightly SPARSER near
the corner before any refinement); the final adaptive mesh's ratio is
29.17 -- a 55.8x growth, direct evidence the estimator concentrated
refinement exactly where the singularity is, not merely producing a
better slope through some other mechanism.

expected_behavior.name: adaptive-beats-uniform-rate
expected_behavior.en: The adaptive (AMR) energy-norm convergence rate is at least 0.10 steeper than the uniform rate, and lands within [-1.0, -0.45] -- near the theoretical optimal -0.5, well past uniform's -1/3 cap.
expected_behavior.rationale: Uniform refinement on this singular problem is provably capped near O(dofs^-1/3) by the corner's limited regularity (theoretical -0.333; achieved -0.338). A working adaptive scheme should recover close to the optimal O(dofs^-1/2) (achieved -0.528) -- a rate ceiling uniform refinement structurally cannot reach on this domain, however many levels it runs. The 0.10 separation margin and the -0.45 ceiling both sit with headroom below the achieved -0.528, ruling out both "no real difference" and "not actually near-optimal" failure modes.

expected_behavior.name: refinement-concentrates-at-corner
expected_behavior.en: The adaptive mesh's final near-corner/far-field cell-density ratio is at least 15x, and has grown at least 10x relative to the initial (near-uniform) mesh's ratio.
expected_behavior.rationale: A better convergence RATE alone doesn't prove the estimator is doing the geometrically sensible thing -- this is the direct structural check. The initial coarse mesh's near/far density ratio is 0.52 (no corner bias); the achieved final adaptive ratio is 29.17 (55.8x growth). 15x/10x thresholds sit with comfortable headroom below both achieved numbers while still failing a scheme that refined uniformly or diffusely instead of concentrating at the singularity.

behavior_tests.name: adaptive-beats-uniform-rate
behavior_tests.description:
The adaptive log-log energy-error-vs-DOFs slope must be <= -0.45 (near
the theoretical optimal -0.5) AND at least 0.10 steeper (more negative)
than the uniform slope over the same initial mesh.

provenance.note: Standard a priori FEM theory for a corner singularity of exponent 2/3 caps P1 uniform refinement's energy-norm rate near O(dofs^-1/3) (theoretical -0.333); optimally graded/adaptive refinement recovers close to the smooth-solution rate O(dofs^-1/2). -0.45 is a calibration margin above (i.e. less steep than) the theoretical -0.5, not a fitted threshold; the achieved production rate is -0.528.

behavior_tests.name: refinement-concentrates-at-corner
behavior_tests.description:
The final adaptive mesh's near-corner (r<0.15) vs far-field (r>0.5)
cell-density ratio must be >= 15.0, and its growth relative to the
initial mesh's ratio must be >= 10.0x.

provenance.note: The initial (near-uniform, pre-refinement) mesh's own near/far density ratio is 0.52 -- the natural "no bias" baseline for this domain/radii choice. The achieved production adaptive mesh's ratio is 29.17 (55.8x growth). 15.0 sits with large headroom below that achieved value while still failing a scheme that spread refinement uniformly (which would keep the ratio near the initial ~0.5).

pipeline_gate.proceed_condition:
No downstream studies in this investigation depend on mesh-convergence;
it stands alongside the investigation's other studies as a standalone
FEM-rigor showcase built directly on the validated dolfinx bridge
(poisson-validation).
